newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks extend losses, sink as techs tumble.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks extend losses, sink as techs tumble.

text.p: Wall Street shares extended sharp losses on Friday morning, tumbling as the technology sector sank amid profit-taking and earnings disappointments.
The Dow Jones Industrial average, which hit fresh highs this week, shed around 124 points, or 1.54 percent, to 7897.
The Nasdaq composite sank around 33 points, or over two percent, to 1536. Technology stocks were battered by profit-taking, after Microsoft Corp reported earnings which were viewed as disappointing.

The New York Stock Exchange, which set curbs on index-arbitrage trading, said its sidecar curbs also went into effect at 1006 EDT/1406 GMT, after the Standard & Poor's 500 futures index fell 12 points.
The Standard & Poor's 500 index lost 16.44 to 915.27.

"The market is in general profit-taking mode in names which have done exceedingly well in recent weeks," Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd, said. "It's volatile. When you have stocks which have gone up 10 points in a week, they will correct with equal velocity."
Microsoft stock sank 8-7/8 to 140-5/8, after reporting fourth quarter earnings of $0.80 per share compared with $0.59 per share in the previous quarter.
Its earnings were slightly better than the First Call consensus estimate of $0.79 per share but well below the so-called "whisper numbers."
"Microsoft was the catalyst on the downside," Bleier said.
Shares of chipmaker Intel Corp lost 2-3/16 to 85-5/8. Compaq Computer Corp fell 4-1/2 to 127-9/16.
But International Business Machines Corp, due to post results Monday, rose. Merrill raised its target on IBM.
